No action this turn. Scope is agreed, so I'll move to the next open part before any approaches.

Good, the scope stands. The next part is what counts as "out of range," because that drives most of the alert logic.

One thing I noticed while reading, which I'll come back to later. The alerting service will read `greenhouse.db` on the same machine that runs `ingest/`. If a January storm cuts power to that machine, no text goes out. A heater failure and a power cut can be the same event. We may want a check that runs from outside the greenhouse.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The 10-minute stale-sensor alert catches one dead sensor. It can't catch a dead alerting service, because a service that is down can't report its own silence.
- The usual fix is a heartbeat. The service checks in with something external every few minutes. That external thing texts you when the check-ins stop.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

The limits come first, though. Fixed limits can sit in a config file. Limits that change by zone or by season need somewhere you can edit them.

What reading would make you want to be woken up, and where do those numbers come from today?
